### Module(s)

tests

### Description

mini.nvim contains a couple files that differ only in case.

The default macOS filesystem is case-insensitive, and changing it would require both reformatting the partition and potentially breaking apps that expect $HOME to be case-insensitive.

As a result, it is impossible to update mini.nvim. My guess is that even with filenames changed in this repo, it'll require manually deleting the mini.nvim plugin and cloning it again.

### Neovim version

*

### Steps to reproduce

Simply cloning the repo on macOS will produce warnings. Pulling then becomes impossible.

### Expected behavior

_No response_

Would you mind checking if this works?

I am working on setting up Continuous Integration for both Windows and MacOS to avoid this kind of errors in the future.
Off topic: very nice Neovim config you have there, by the way.

Hard reset and pull worked perfectly. Thanks!

Re: my config, thank you very much! I'm proud of it. I'm curious, when you were looking at it, did anything seem familiar? Things like placing utility functions in a namespace with my initials?

`mini.nvim` is not just amazingly useful (I mean, a completion plugin that works perfectly with only `require('mini.completion').setup()` is life-changing and I don't know why this isn't the single most-starred plugin), it's also a reference for outstanding coding technique. Your code is elegant and brilliant, and I've learned a tremendous amount from you.

Closing then.

Don't make me blush :) I did, in fact, notice `_G.AW = {}` but don't claim that was my original idea. I might have seen it somewhere else.

Some tips:
- Having namespaced config via subdirectory in 'lua' should be more stable in long term. It reduces possibility of module name collisions inside `require()` (like what if some plugin wanted to use `require('windows')`, for example?).
- Using `local H = {}` for local helper functions is, strictly speaking, unnecessary if you define all its elements before they are used. Main reason why I use this approach here is to first define exported functionality and only after that - local helpers. For me proved to be a better code organization with a negligible overhead.
